title: Integral constructible internal Hom
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ and $\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ on the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ambient derived category of $\widehat R_X$-modules, with the full subcategory $D^b_c(X,R)$ of derived-complete complexes whose finite reductions are bounded constructible and have cohomological supports in one interval independent of $n$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For an ambient complex $M$ write $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ for its reduction in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].

For every $K,L\in D^b_c(X,R)$, their ambient derived internal Hom $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$. For every $n\geq1$ the canonical evaluation-defined comparison is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$,
$$
 H_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(K_n,L_n).
$$
More precisely, let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq e$ be integers and $d\geq0$ an integer with $\dim X\leq d$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $(A_n)_X$ and every $L_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,e]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], then every $H_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$, uniformly in $n$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $K$ and $L$ are derived complete, and $K_1,L_1$ are bounded constructible. Choose integers $\alpha\leq\beta$ and $\gamma\leq\epsilon$ containing their respective cohomological supports; the zero complex permits any such interval. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] separately to $K$ and $L$. It gives Tor amplitude $[\alpha,\beta]$ for every $K_n$ and $[\gamma,\epsilon]$ for every $L_n$. The coefficient ring is the stipulated DVR $\mathcal O_E$, and $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ because $X$ is over a field of characteristic $p\ne\ell$. The reductions are therefore finite-Tor bounded constructible complexes on the pro-etale site.

source.place: ## Proof, second sentence: input reductions are finite-Tor

proof.text: Set $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,L)$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] in the ambient category of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf. Since $L$ is derived complete, $H$ is derived complete. For each $n\geq1$ the same lemma gives the canonical evaluation-defined, $A_n$-linear isomorphism $H_n\cong R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(K_n,L_n)$. This is exactly the reduction assertion of the item; no perfectness of $K$ on the entire site is required.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: completeness and canonical reductions

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is of finite type over the field $k$, so [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives $\dim X<\infty$. With dimension as the supremum of finite lengths of chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], choose an integer $d_0\geq0$ with $\dim X\leq d_0$; for $X=\emptyset$, whose dimension is $-\infty$, take $d_0=0$. This bound depends only on $X$, not on the reduction level.

source.place: ## Proof, third sentence: a fixed dimension bound for the uniform finite-level estimate

proof.text: For every $n\geq1$, apply the pro-etale assertion of [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] to $K_n,L_n$, with $A=A_{E,n}$ and the intervals from step 1. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is separated finite type over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, the torsion prime is different from $p$, and both input reductions are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Thus $R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(K_n,L_n)$ is bounded constructible, with Tor amplitude in $[\gamma-\beta-2d_0,\epsilon-\alpha+2d_0]$. By the isomorphism in step 2, this is also true of $H_n$. The same application with any supplied intervals $[a,b],[c,e]$ and any supplied dimension bound $d$ yields $[c-b-2d,e-a+2d]$, proving the quantitative clause. All these are Tor intervals over $A_n$, without changing to Tor amplitude after restriction to $R$.

source.place: ## Proof, third sentence: constructibility and the stated uniform bound

proof.text: Write $u=\gamma-\beta-2d_0$ and $v=\epsilon-\alpha+2d_0$, so $u\leq v$. In the definition of Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], take the degree-zero sheaf $M=(A_n)_X$. To see that this tests the cohomology of $H_n$ itself, use a K-flat representative $P\to H_n$ as in [def-weil-derived-tensor]: the degreewise maps $P\otimes_{(A_n)_X}(A_n)_X\to P$, $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, commute with differentials. Hence $H_n\otimes^L_{A_n}(A_n)_X\cong H_n$, and $\mathcal H^i(H_n)=0$ outside $[u,v]$ for every $n$. Step 2 gives derived completeness, and step 4 gives bounded constructibility of every reduction. Together with this single cohomological interval, these are precisely the three conditions defining $H\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].
